Hassel Lecture 2026: A stereochemical journey
May 21, 2026 3:42 PM
Professor Jérôme Lacour from the Université de Genève visited the Department of Chemistry this week as the Hassel Lecturer, a lecture series held in honour of Nobel laureate Odd Hassel. In two talks, Lacour presented both fundamental and cutting‑edge research in stereochemistry, reactive carbenes, and asymmetric synthesis.

A chemical retrospective as the institute prepares for convergence research environments and the Life Sciences Building
Dec. 17, 2025 12:46 PM
The Department of Chemistry made history in 1969 when Odd Hassel was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Together with skilled colleagues he helped develop an electron-diffraction apparatus capable of imaging chemical structures. Since then, the department has nurtured many strong research groups. Now the institute is entering a new phase as it prepares to move into the Life Sciences Building.
Convergence Environment Receives 17 million in Funding to Address Societal Challenges in Health
Nov. 7, 2025 11:14 AM
The funding is for research to develop new medications for bacterial infections and cancer. The purpose of convergence environments is to promote interdisciplinary collaboration among researchers at the Life Sciences Building and other researchers at the University of Oslo (UiO). One of eight such environments will be led by Professor Reidar Lund from the Department of Chemistry. The funding is for a period of four years.
